heuristics: H1: the class-level r-adding walk with 2^16 adders behaves as a random mapping on the (r-1)/6 order-6 classes, up to an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16.
H2: fruitless 2-cycles occur at rate at most 2^-16 per step and 3..64-cycles at rate at most 2^-32 per step.

H3: Callgrind instruction counts on 2^18 sampled secp256k1 walk steps on each of two input sets represent per-step work; every instruction is charged (no reference operation), 795 against 780.0 measured.
limitations: The model success bound is 0.411523 at tau = 0.5303, 0.0215 above 0.39; pooled toy-curve success at that budget is in the evidence.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution.
Needs about 2^67.7 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
All field arithmetic is the package's own inline assembly, tested against Python big integers but not formally verified.
H1 is an unproved standard heuristic; the whole procedure, including resolution, is tested only on toy curves.
Distinguished points never occur in a production-parameter measurement sample; the restart and abandonment paths were checked on small builds.
